Both appends now open with `forUpdating:`, check the last byte, and prepend a newline only when the file is non-empty and doesn't end in 0x0A. That matches the request. The session tests cover the torn-line case from the request and the newline-terminated case. The suite passed (216 tests). The WireLog change is untested, which the agent disclosed.

All four JSONL readers (read_results, read_lines, Journal.read, and the journal lookup in load_run_config) now split on "\n" only. The blank-line and torn-tail handling is unchanged, so a trailing newline adds no record. The new tests cover each reader. The only flaw is that two of the parametrized control-character cases test nothing.

The shared helper `read_jsonl_lines` splits on "\n" only, drops the empty trailing element, and is used by all four readers (`read_results`, `read_lines`, `Journal.read`, `load_run_config`). Blank-line skipping and torn-tail handling are unchanged. The one weakness is a regression test that does not exercise the fix.

The change splits on "\n" in read_results, export.read_lines, Journal.read and the config.py journal lookup. It uses the last non-blank line for the torn-tail check, so trailing newlines, blank lines, torn tails and mid-file corruption behave as asked. The tests cover the examples from the request. The only gap I found is that the config.py change has no test.

The change does what was asked. `apply_patch` is now an editor, and the call's paths come from `PatchParser` and `EditFileTool.paths`, which the tool's own `path` function now uses. Deny and ask match on any path, and allow needs all of them. The three patch scenarios from the request are tested, and the report is candid about what it left unchecked. The remaining gaps are minor: the test only covers `Add File` patches, and an unparseable patch matches no rule.

The `steady` logic follows the stated rules: the 3x threshold, pending and 6h confirmation, the clock restart, return to the old price, and keeping servers apart. Two gaps remain. The third-party-only gating is not in `price`/`priceNoted`, and the agent's claim that it is isn't supported by the diff. Persistence and the version-string note are mostly untested.

The change in both SessionStore.append and WireLog.writeContext looks correct. It opens the file read+write, seeks to the last byte, and writes a newline only if the file is non-empty and doesn't end in one. After that it seeks to the end and appends. Empty and newline-terminated files get no extra bytes. The only gap is that no tests were added for the new behavior.

Both `SessionStore.append(_:to:)` and `WireLog.writeContext` now check the file's last byte through a separate read handle. They write a newline first only if the file is non-empty and doesn't end in 0x0A. This matches the request, and empty files and files already ending in a newline get nothing extra. The one gap is that no regression test was added.

The change does what was asked. `SessionStore.append` and the `WireLog` index append both go through a shared helper, `seekToEndOfJSONL()`. The helper returns a newline only when the file is non-empty and its last byte isn't `\n`, so empty and well-formed files get nothing extra. The switch to `FileHandle(forUpdating:)` is needed to read the last byte, and the file exists at both call sites. The new tests cover the torn-line scenario from the request, the no-extra-blank-line case, and the wire log index. The agent reports the suite passing, which I could not re-run.

The diff does what was asked. RateLimits has the shared instance, a public init, and per-host windows for the three limits. It matches header names case-insensitively, parses ISO 8601 dates with and without fractions, and replaces a limit's window without touching the others. `pause` uses the right thresholds (requests ≤ 0, token limits < 1,000) and the 60 s cap. ChatClient waits before the request and records each response's headers. The 404 message keeps the server text and appends "The server doesn't offer <model>. Pick another model." The retry order is Retry-After, then the body's `retryDelay`, then the fixed backoff. The agent's report matches the diff.

The change replaces `splitlines()` with a `"\n"`-only `split_jsonl` helper in all four JSONL readers: `Journal.read`, `export.read_lines`, `job.read_results` and the journal lookup in `load_run_config`. Blank-line skipping, torn-tail tolerance and the mid-file `ValueError` stay as they were. The new tests cover U+2028, U+2029, U+0085, a trailing newline, blank lines, a torn tail and a corrupt middle line. I couldn't confirm the agent's claim that the remaining `splitlines` calls in `cli.py`, `display.py`, `preflight.py` and `config.py:118` read non-JSONL data, because their code isn't in the diff. I found no problems in the diff.

The diff covers the request: the RateLimits actor, the pause before requests and retries, recording of response headers, the body retryDelay with the right precedence, and the 404 hint. I found no functional bugs. The new logic is untested, and a retry can wait twice on the same reset.

Both `SessionStore.append` and `WireLog.writeContext` now open the file read-write (`forUpdating`). If the file is non-empty, they check the last byte after seeking to the end. If it isn't 0x0A, they write a newline before the new record. An empty file or one that already ends in a newline gets nothing extra, which matches the request. After the one-byte read the file position is back at the end, so the writes land in the right place. I found no correctness problems in the diff, but it adds no tests.

The change implements the requested behavior. Stale unfinished redo jobs are superseded when their limit or their item set differs. The log messages use the exact wording and count only ok answers. Replanning leaves out prompts any redo job already answered. A SUT with no items only has its stale job superseded, and a job that is not stale resumes as before. The tests cover the example and the edge cases. The one deviation from the request, the adjusted items comparison, is disclosed and reasonable.

The change does what was asked. `edit_file` now resolves `file_path` and `edits[].path` through a shared `EditFileTool.paths` helper, and `apply_patch` paths come from `PatchParser` and `PatchOp.paths`, so Move-to targets and Delete File are included. Deny and ask rules match on any path and allow rules need all of them. The nil and root-search cases are kept. The new test covers the three scenarios in the request, and the suite passed.

The change swaps `splitlines()` for `split("\n")` in the four JSONL readers the agent named: `read_results`, `read_lines`, `Journal.read` and the journal lookup in `load_run_config`. That fixes the described bug and keeps blank-line skipping. I could not check whether any other readers exist, and no test covers the new behaviour.

The code change looks correct for both SessionStore.append and WireLog, and the new test covers the torn-line case. The report's central claim, that the suite passed with exit 0, conflicts with the recorded check, which shows `sh run-tests.sh` exiting 1.
